narrative:
The model determined that you have an 86% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and your property ownership situation. 

Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only about 13% have accounts in the red, while the majority maintain positive balances or no account at all. This negative status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

Your credit history of having all previous credits paid back at this bank also worked against you. This is quite uncommon—only 3% of approved applicants share this history—making it the second strongest factor increasing your risk score.

Finally, having no known property or assets was the third most important driver. Most successful applicants own a car, real estate, or have some form of insurance or savings that can serve as collateral. The absence of any such assets further increased the model's concern.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a positive checking account balance, reducing your overall debt load, and acquiring some form of tangible assets. Consider reapplying once these areas show clear improvement. (218 words)
